doc.title: Ann Rabson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 21, 2007

title: Club pay of fifty bucks and a career better than expected
summary: A club date paid fifty dollars; she credits the blues revival, learning piano and good management for a career beyond her expectations.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Okay. What would a club date pay back then, if you could get one?

If you could get one fifty bucks. And you know, they probably still pay fifty bucks. I mean I’ve had a lot — people say oh you’re a woman and has it been hard. I don’t know. But the truth is I’ve had a lot of — it’s hard to say that anything’s hurt my career because my career is so much better than I ever expected it would be. And I expected I’d always

be playing for fifty bucks, and having all that trouble. And really the blues revival and well the fact that I learned to play the piano too, that helped. And I’ve had wonderful management and I’ve learned. I mean I love music.
